chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all of them, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'd, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'When the funeral is being carried out and I am not in a state of ablution, if I go to perform ablution, I will miss the funeral prayer. Will it suffice for me to pray over it while I am not in a state of ablution?' He said: 'It is more beloved to me that you be in a state of purity.'

And this narration includes that purity is superior, and it indicates that non-purity is also permissible, and it is permissible for a person to perform dry ablution (tayammum) instead of purity if he fears missing the prayer. This was narrated.
ai.seo_question: Is it valid to pray the funeral prayer without wudu if you might miss the congregation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of validity versus preference in funeral prayers, establishing that while ritual purity (wudu) is superior, the prayer remains valid without it to prevent missing the congregational prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *takhfif* (easing) in times of necessity, explicitly permitting tayammum as a valid substitute for wudu when water is scarce or time is critical, thereby prioritizing the performance of the act over its ideal conditions.
